paragraph: Multi-family is the center of the Fairview market, with 13 sales over six months at a median of $800,000 and a sale-to-list ratio of 1.032. Roughly three quarters of those closed above asking with a median of 22 days on market, so sellers of two and three family properties are largely getting their number, and buyers competing for them should not expect much room. Detached single-family is thinner at 6 sales and a median of $645,000, half above asking, also 22 days on market. Competitive, not frenzied. Condos and townhouses run the other way: 9 sales at a median of $545,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 0.976, and 34 days on market, with only one in nine going above list. That tier is where a buyer has actual negotiating room. The condo range runs from $279,000 to $780,000, so the median is the better guide than either end. On the monthly numbers, no tier posts more than three closings in any single month, which is too small a sample to read a trend from. Judge Fairview on the six-month picture. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the rental income of a multi-family, the space and grounds of a single-family, or the lower price point and lighter upkeep of a condo.
